channel.title: TribalGaming.com — News & Analysis
channel.description: Authoritative news and analysis of tribal gaming in the United States and Canada.

item.title: Coushatta Casino Resort opens Legacy Tower in Louisiana expansion
item.description: The Coushatta Tribe of Louisiana opened its 204-room Legacy Tower this month, capping the most significant capital project in the resort's 30-year history.

item.title: California tribes formally defer sports betting ballot to 2028
item.description: California's gaming tribes have ruled out a 2026 sports-betting ballot, citing intra-tribal coalition work and a need to settle revenue-sharing with non-gaming tribes first.

item.title: DOI Part 293, two years in: how the new compact rules reshaped tribal-state talks
item.description: The Department of the Interior's 2024 update to 25 C.F.R. Part 293 has quietly become one of the most consequential federal actions on tribal gaming in a decade.

item.title: British Columbia's First Nations casino buyouts: a quiet ownership shift
item.description: Eight commercial casinos in southwest British Columbia have transferred to First Nations ownership in two years, reshaping Canadian gaming structure.

item.title: Beyond the casinos: how the Chickasaw Nation built a diversified enterprise
item.description: The Chickasaw Nation operates 18 Oklahoma casinos and more than 100 other businesses. The non-gaming portfolio is where the tribe's long game shows up.

item.title: Catawba Two Kings Casino opens first phase of $1B North Carolina resort
item.description: The Catawba Nation opened phase one of its $1 billion Two Kings Casino Resort in Kings Mountain, North Carolina — 1,350 slots, 22 tables, sports betting kiosks.

item.title: New Mexico tribes sue Kalshi, alleging IGRA violations on tribal lands
item.description: Four New Mexico tribes filed federal suit against Kalshi, arguing the platform's sports event contracts are unauthorized Class III gaming under IGRA.

item.title: Alberta iGaming launches July 13 — what 2% revenue sharing means for First Nations
item.description: Alberta's regulated iGaming market opens July 13, 2026, with 28 operators and a 2% gross revenue allocation to First Nations. A closer look at the framework.

item.title: Prediction markets and tribal exclusivity — IGRA's biggest 2026 stress test
item.description: Tribal lawsuits against Kalshi and Polymarket have made prediction markets the most consequential challenge to IGRA exclusivity in 2026. An analysis.

item.title: Class II vs Class III tribal gaming — what the IGRA distinction actually means
item.description: Class II vs Class III gaming under IGRA is one of the most consequential distinctions in tribal gaming law. A clear, operator-focused explainer.

item.title: Inside the Seminole Compact: How one 30-year deal reshaped American sports betting
item.description: An exclusive analysis of the hub-and-spoke framework now drawing legal challenges in four other states — and why tribal attorneys say IGRA has always anticipated this moment.

item.title: Tribal gaming generated $138B in total economic output in 2025, new report finds
item.description: The most comprehensive joint AGA–NIGA assessment to date.

item.title: SIGA announces seventh property as Saskatchewan First Nations drive provincial gaming
item.description: The Saskatchewan Indian Gaming Authority remains the dominant model for First Nations gaming in Canada.
